chapter: Family and early memories of Jelly
title: Not seeing Jelly again until 1925; family differences
summary: She did not see him from about 1906 until 1925, no memory of a 1918 visit, and talks about her sister and her own family.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, do you remember seeing your brother then any other time after, say, around 1906, when he was six years old, until you went and she called him?
25, 1925 or nothing. Well, I saw him again. He was sick.
Your sister tells about that the only time she really heard him play, he came here in 1918. Now, you would have been 18 years old then. I don't remember him.
You don't remember that business? No.
Because I got married in 1918. So maybe you were busy and gone.

I might have. And then I'm going to tell you, our family are peculiar people. If—if my—now, my sister was very, very selfish. She tried to keep her children and her husband, everybody to herself. And I was just different. My first husband and I separated. But my son knows all of his aunts. He has eight aunts and three uncles. And real and truly, he's down there with them now. Married, he's down there with them. His daughter lives next to his father. And as much as we separated, I didn't want to separate the family, you know what I mean? No. My son went to see his father every holiday. Every other Saturday, he'd go down to see him. And he never paid Alamone either. I took care of him now. Then you didn't see your brother then until 1925? I didn't see my brother until 1925, that I can remember.
